issues.description: Interface name mismatch: the problem statement and the template Main expect an interface named `Rideable` declaring a method `messageOnRide()`. The solution repository instead provides an interface `Mountable` (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) that declares `messageOnRide()`, and the classes Pig and Seal implement `Mountable`. Meanwhile, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java in the solution is empty. This inconsistent identifier naming (Rideable vs Mountable) makes it unclear which interface students should implement and will break direct reuse of the solution or the template Main: code referring to `Rideable` will not match classes that implement `Mountable`, causing compilation errors or confusion about the intended interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface identifier consistent across all artifacts. Options: (a) Rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java (update its package and filename) and update Pig and Seal to implement `Rideable` so the solution matches the problem statement and template; or (b) implement a proper Rideable.java in the solution that declares `String messageOnRide()` and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable (or have Rideable extend Mountable as a compatibility shim). Ensure the problem statement, template Main, and solution all reference the same interface name (`Rideable`) so students know which interface to implement and so code compiles without renaming.

issues.description: The exercise specifies an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide() (problem statement and template), but the solution implements that concept as an interface named 'Mountable' (Mountable.java) and has an empty Rideable.java file. Specifically: the problem statement/UML calls the interface 'Rideable'; the template Main.java references 'Rideable' in example usage; the solution defines 'Mountable' (with messageOnRide()) and has an empty Rideable.java. This naming mismatch prevents students from directly mapping the required interface name to the provided solution code and may block or confuse them when implementing or referencing the interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Best fix: replace Mountable.java with Rideable.java (declare 'public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }'), update all solution classes (Pig, Seal, etc.) to implement Rideable instead of Mountable, and remove or repurpose the empty Rideable.java file so the interface name matches the problem statement and template. Alternatively, if Mountable is preferred, update the problem statement and template to reference 'Mountable' everywhere. Ensure only one interface file with the intended name exists.
